ak_ravine_lake_main_walls.blurb: The Main Walls are the section of the Ravine Lake cliffs nearest the road, in the Mat-Su Valley off the Glenn Highway. About twenty routes mix traditional leads with a smaller number of bolted ones, and a couple of the bolted lines go two pitches. Grades start around 5.7, and the bulk are 5.10, with a few 5.11 and one 5.12 for stronger leaders. Expect cracks, corners, roofs and arêtes on textured, somewhat gritty rock. With so many lines packed into one short wall, it makes a good half day of mixed leading.

ak_monolith_the.blurb: The Monolith is one of the named technical climbing formations in Archangel Valley, in the Hatcher Pass area north of Anchorage. Most of the twenty routes are traditional, with a few bolted lines. They run from easy fifth class through a cluster of 5.7 to 5.9 moderates to about half a dozen 5.10s and two 5.11s. Rock in the valley is blocky granite that collects moss, and spring and fall rain keep it growing, so plan for some vegetation. The road in is rough on cars, and a four-wheel-drive vehicle is needed beyond the Reed Lakes trailhead lot.

ak_green_gully.blurb: Green Gully is the prominent gully left of the Diamond in Archangel Valley, part of the Hatcher Pass climbing zone north of Anchorage. Nearly everything here is traditional protection, with only a single bolted line, and the difficulty runs high for a crag this size. Most routes are 5.10 or 5.11, with several 5.12s and just two at 5.9. Some are two pitches, and at least one has a runout section. To get in, cross the boulder field below the Diamond and then bear left for roughly a quarter mile. This is a place for confident trad leaders.

ab_house_of_cards.blurb: House of Cards is a large limestone wall in Cougar Canyon in the Bow Valley near Canmore, offering sport climbing only. Roughly thirty routes run from 5.8 up to the low 5.11s, and about half sit at 5.10, so it suits climbers who already lead that grade. Parts of the wall are taller than 45 metres and shaped like a pyramid. It gets sun in the morning, and the creek in the canyon rises during the melt season. Late spring through early fall is the usual window. Check current notices about worn bolt hardware before you go.

ab_mount_baldy_crag.blurb: Mount Baldy Crag is a sport-only crag in Kananaskis, Alberta, with just under thirty routes. The lines are short single pitches, many in the 50 to 70 foot range, with bolted anchors. The grade spread is unusually wide for its size: a few routes at 5.4 to 5.6, a middle group at 5.7 to 5.9, and the largest share at 5.10, with one 5.11. That makes it a useful choice for newer leaders who want some gentle options, as well as climbers looking for quick, compact pitches. The wall can feel slick when damp.

ab_paddock_wall.blurb: Paddock Wall is a sector of Sunshine Rock in Banff National Park, Alberta, with sport climbing that starts almost at the car; the walk takes about a minute. Routes are well bolted on solid rock, mostly vertical faces on good holds, with some steeper sections added in recent years. Of the twenty-seven lines, most are 5.10 or 5.11, a few are 5.7 to 5.9, and one is 5.12, so it fits climbers comfortable leading 5.10 better than beginners. It works well as a quick stop for several pitches when time is short.
